18:59 Local Time, 14:59 GMT, 20:29 IST: An exceptional bowling performance from Afghanistan. Yes, it's a used pitch and not the easiest surface to bat on, but this certainly wasn't a 169-all-out wicket. The pacers, Fazalhaq and Omarzai, set the tone by picking up three wickets in the powerplay. Taylor fell soon after, leaving Zimbabwe reeling at 55/4, before Raza and Burl joined forces to steady the innings. The pair rotated the strike well and picked up the odd boundary, but the introduction of Nabi put the brakes on the scoring and eventually led to Burl's dismissal. That opened the door for Rashid Khan, who ran through the lower order, picking up the next three wickets, including the crucial scalp of Raza, who fought a lone battle with a 68. The last wicket stand did frustrate Afghanistan, adding 32 valuable runs, but Zimbabwe have still finished with a below-par total. Afghanistan will back themselves to chase this down.
